pr.title: Remove unneeded `drop_in_place` calls
pr.description:
Might as well pull this out from rust-lang/rust#144561 because this is still used in things like `Vec::truncate` where it'd be nice to allow it be removed if inlined enough to see that the type is `Copy`.

So long as perf says it's ok, at least 🤞
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: The PR is a missed-optimization improvement, not a semantic miscompile. Before the PR, RemoveUnneededDrops only rewrote `Drop` terminators and left `drop_in_place::<T>` calls for non-drop types intact; after the PR it rewrites those calls to `goto` when `T::needs_drop` is false. For the focused case `T = [char]`, the call has no observable effect, so old and new behavior are observationally identical. There is no historically justified wrong transformation that changes values, and producing a differential counterexample would require fabricating an unrelated unsound rewrite (e.g., erasing a `drop_in_place` for a type that needs dropping), which this PR does not do.

analysis.summary: RemoveUnneededDrops was extended from rewriting only `Drop` terminators to also rewrite `drop_in_place::<T>` call terminators into `goto` when `T` does not need dropping, but only at `mir-opt-level > 0` and only when the callee is the `DropInPlace` lang item. The reusable correctness boundary is: remove the call iff the lang-item type argument `T` satisfies `!needs_drop`, and preserve the unwind/CFG behavior. The test uses a direct `std::ptr::drop_in_place` on a `[char]` pointer and checks that the call and its continuation block disappear.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `RemoveUnneededDrops` only inspected `TerminatorKind::Drop { place, target, .. }`; it obtained the dropped type from `place.ty(&body.local_decls, tcx)`, checked `ty.ty.needs_drop(tcx, typing_env)`, and if false replaced the terminator with `TerminatorKind::Goto { target }`. Calls to `drop_in_place` were not considered, so a `TerminatorKind::Call` to `drop_in_place::<T>` remained even when `T` was `Copy`/did not need drop. The PR notes that such calls are "common in generic code (such as `Vec::truncate`)" and that removing them "from things like inlined `Vec<u8>` is helpful".
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical pre-PR transformation is a missed optimization rather than a miscompile: it left `TerminatorKind::Call` terminators invoking `drop_in_place::<T>` untouched even when `T` does not need dropping, so a function containing only such a call still had a call/continuation block instead of a straight-line `goto`/return. The new behavior must not be generalized into an unsound rewrite: it is not correct to erase every `drop_in_place` call, nor to erase it when `T::needs_drop` is true, nor to ignore the `mir_opt_level() > 0` gate. The patch specifically matches `TerminatorKind::Call { ref func, target: Some(target), .. }` where `func.const_fn_def()` yields `(def_id, generics)` and `tcx.is_lang_item(def_id, LangItem::DropInPlace)`, then takes the dropped type from `generics.type_at(0)` rather than from the pointer argument, checks `if ty.needs_drop(tcx, typing_env) { continue; }`, and otherwise sets `terminator.kind = TerminatorKind::Goto { target }`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies at `tcx.sess.mir_opt_level() > 0` containing a `TerminatorKind::Call` whose callee is the `DropInPlace` lang item (`std::ptr::drop_in_place`) with a resolvable constant function definition, a `Some` normal-return target, and a first generic type argument `T` for which `T::needs_drop(tcx, typing_env)` is false. The focused example is an `unsafe fn slice_in_place(ptr: *mut [char])` calling `std::ptr::drop_in_place(ptr)`, i.e. `T = [char]`, built with `-Z mir-opt-level=1`; the type is not `Copy` in the strict trait sense but still does not need dropping. Negative-domain controls are the same shape with a `T` that does need dropping, and the same `drop_in_place` call at `mir-opt-level=0`.
analysis.trigger: A call terminator to the `DropInPlace` lang item at optimization level greater than zero, where the call's first generic type argument has `needs_drop == false`. The pass source describes the motivation: "When we're optimizing, we also remove calls to `drop_in_place<T>` when `T` isn't `needs_drop`, as those are essentially equivalent to `Drop` terminators."
preconditions: `tcx.sess.mir_opt_level() > 0`; the old pass ran regardless, but the new `drop_in_place` rewrite is explicitly optimization-gated.
The terminator must be `TerminatorKind::Call { ref func, target: Some(target), .. }`; calls without a normal-return target do not match.
`func.const_fn_def()` must return `Some((def_id, generics))`, and `tcx.is_lang_item(def_id, LangItem::DropInPlace)` must hold.
The dropped type is `generics.type_at(0)`, the type parameter of `drop_in_place<T>`, not the type of the pointer argument.
`ty.needs_drop(tcx, typing_env)` must be false; if true the pass must `continue` and leave the call.
The succeeding transformation replaces the call terminator with `TerminatorKind::Goto { target }`, preserving the normal-return target and dropping the call/unwind behavior.
pitfalls: Do not remove `drop_in_place<T>` when `T::needs_drop` is true; that would skip required destructor behavior.
Do not derive the type from the pointer argument (`*mut [char]`); use `generics.type_at(0)` (`[char]`). These can differ in drop requirements.
Do not apply the rewrite at `mir-opt-level=0`; the patch gates it on `mir_opt_level() > 0`.
Only match the `DropInPlace` lang item and a `const_fn_def`; arbitrary calls named similarly or non-lang-item functions must not be erased.

The call terminator includes an unwind edge (`drop_in_place ... -> [return: bb1, unwind continue]`); replacing with `goto` removes the continuation/unwind path, so the CFG must be simplified consistently (`should_simplify`).
The test is marked `//@ needs-unwind`; the generated MIR for `drop_in_place` includes explicit unwind/return structure, so the expected diff must account for the removed continuation block.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a mir-opt test with `//@ test-mir-pass: RemoveUnneededDrops`, `//@ needs-unwind`, and `//@ compile-flags: -Z mir-opt-level=1`, emitting `// EMIT_MIR remove_unneeded_drop_in_place.slice_in_place.RemoveUnneededDrops.diff`. The regression test defines `unsafe fn slice_in_place(ptr: *mut [char]) { std::ptr::drop_in_place(ptr) }` and invokes it from `main` on a `['o', 'k']` array via `&raw mut`. The expected before-MIR contains `_0 = drop_in_place::<[char]>(move _2) -> [return: bb1, unwind continue];` plus `bb1: { StorageDead(_2); return; }`; the expected after-MIR removes the call and `bb1`, leaving `StorageLive(_2); _2 = copy _1; StorageDead(_2); return;` in `bb0`. For a two-program differential harness, keep the same function but change only whether `drop_in_place` is replaced by straight-line `goto`/return: with a non-drop type the call should disappear; with a type that needs drop it must remain. Add a control at `-Z mir-opt-level=0` where the call must remain, and a positive type with a real destructor to guard against an unconditional erasure. No compiler was built or run for this analysis; these are source-derived expectations from the supplied diff.
evidence: //! When we're optimizing, we also remove calls to `drop_in_place<T>` when `T` isn't `needs_drop`,
//! `Vec::truncate`) so removing them from things like inlined `Vec<u8>` is helpful.
